findings.anchor: §7.4 (AD-20) — user-presence approval, FIDO floor + downgrade ceremony
findings.detail: Gate 1 D6/AT-PRESENCE-1 only requires, for target-repo policy activation, a verified host-native prompt, else 'a user-configured external signature', else refusal — it does not mandate hardware attestation. Gate 2 imposes a FIDO hardware-presence floor as the default for target-repo activation and then invents a 'one-time downgrade ceremony' plus a perpetual 'every policy status output names the reduced floor for the life of the install' obligation to restore the plainly Gate-1-permitted external-signature path. That is a whole sub-mechanism (bootstrap-authorized ceremony, reduced-floor flagging, §14 disclosure) that exists only to walk back a floor Gate 1 never asked for. The spec itself concedes the point in §14: 'An independent review flagged this as machinery Gate 1 does not require, and that reading is correct.' Note this is distinct from D10/Gate-1 integrity, where the hardware floor IS required. Does not block release; it neither reduces user capability nor leaves a rule uncovered, and it is honestly disclosed.

AT-GATE-3 (the governing case) requires review 'in a fresh session by a different model than the authoring context.' Gate 2's wrapper (AD-29) provably records the *reviewer's* model, but the *authoring* model is the self-declared header field 'Authored by claude-opus-5' — the spec flags it as 'self-declared ... the one link in the D8 chain that is asserted rather than proven.' The different-model check therefore compares one proven operand against one asserted operand, so the contract cannot fail when the authoring model is mislabeled; a same-model author that declares a different model would pass. This is a real hole in the governing case's testable contract, though it is disclosed and is arguably inherent (model identity of authored text is not cryptographically provable). Recorded as a limitation, not a coverage gap.
